author: Mick Cairn

m1.summary: Why AI needs no special skill, and the two exercises that prove it.

m2.summary: Goal-first requests, and why asking for three versions beats asking for one.

m3.summary: Trust it for drafts, verify it for facts. The habit worth more than any prompting trick.

m4.summary: Using AI to think, not just to produce text. Interviews, iteration, pushback.

m5.summary: One real task a day for five days, using the four habits.

addExercises.label: Day 1
addExercises.text: Pick one real task you would normally put off: an email, a decision, a plan, or a piece of research. Use the assistant for it with the four habits. Write down the task and what happened.

addExercises.label: Day 2
addExercises.text: A different real task. This time ask for three versions or three options before you settle on one. Write down which one you picked and why.

addExercises.label: Day 3
addExercises.text: A task with at least one fact in it. Check every fact the assistant gives you against a real source. Write down what held up and what did not.

addExercises.label: Day 4
addExercises.text: A decision or plan. Ask the assistant to interview you about it, one question at a time, before it gives any advice. Write down the question that helped most.

addExercises.label: Day 5
addExercises.text: Your choice. Use all four habits on one task: plain goal, options, verify, iterate. Write down what you would do differently from Day 1.

closing: You have the whole foundation now: it is a conversation, describe the goal and not the mechanism, verify facts, and iterate instead of accepting the first answer.
